designSummary: Case-control study with two controls per case from the same operating list; conditional logistic regression.
sampleSize: With matched prophylaxis in about 55 percent of controls (planning value near the 52 percent reported elsewhere) and an odds ratio of 0.6 for matched prophylaxis compared with under-prophylaxis, 80 percent power at two-sided alpha 0.05 with two controls per case needs about 182 cases and 364 controls, 546 records in all. The nausea log recorded 742 rescue treatments last year, so about nine months of lists supply enough cases; the 18-month window allows cases to be sampled at random. Reading 546 records at about six minutes each takes about 55 hours, within the 60 hours available.
primaryAnalysis: Conditional logistic regression of case status on prophylaxis category (under, matched, over; matched as reference) adjusted for risk score, duration of surgery and opioid dose, reporting odds ratios with 95 percent confidence intervals.
secondaryAnalysis: Logistic regression of sedation delaying discharge on over-prophylaxis among all sampled patients, adjusted for the same variables; adherence among controls with its interval; agreement between the two readers (kappa) on exposure category.
missingData: A missing risk score is reconstructed from recorded factors and flagged; if factors are missing too, the record is kept with a missing-score category and a sensitivity analysis excludes it.
multiplicity: One primary contrast (under versus matched); secondary analyses reported with intervals and labelled as secondary.
software: R with the survival package for conditional logistic regression; extraction form and analysis code archived before reading starts.
overfittingGuards: Three adjustment variables fixed before extraction
About 60 cases per adjustment variable including exposure levels
summary: About 182 cases and 364 controls, about 55 hours of reading; conditional logistic regression with three covariates.
